name: Quinoa
water: Moderate; reduce as seed heads mature
climate: Cool to mild growing season; tolerates dry conditions once established
tip: Harvest when seed heads are dry and seed resists a fingernail.

name: Buckwheat
tip: Fast growing and useful as a short-season crop or green manure.

name: Millet
tip: Allow seed heads to dry before threshing.

name: Sorghum
tip: Plant after soil has warmed and protect young seedlings from frost.

name: Barley
tip: Reduce irrigation as grain ripens and harvest when heads are dry.

name: Oats
tip: Consistent moisture during early growth supports good establishment.

name: Rye
tip: Useful as a winter grain or cover crop.

name: Wheat
tip: Harvest when heads and stems have dried and grain is hard.

name: Rice
water: High and consistent during active growth
climate: Warm-season with a long frost-free period
tip: Home rice can be grown in consistently wet soil; permanent flooding is not essential for every method.

name: Cumin
tip: Avoid excessive humidity as seed heads mature.

name: Caraway
tip: Caraway is commonly biennial; allow plants to overwinter for seed production.

name: Anise
climate: Mild to warm frost-free growing period
tip: Direct sow because established plants dislike root disturbance.

name: Borage
harvest: Leaves and flowers from about 8 weeks
tip: Allow room for its broad, sprawling growth.

name: Chamomile
depth: Surface sow; needs light to germinate
tip: Pick flowers regularly when fully open.

name: Chervil
tip: Sow successively because plants bolt quickly in heat.

name: Hyssop
tip: Trim after flowering to maintain compact growth.

name: Lovage
tip: Allow plenty of space; mature plants can become tall and broad.

name: Savory
climate: Temperate; summer and winter types differ
tip: Harvest leafy tips before heavy flowering for best flavour.

name: Stevia
climate: Warm temperate to subtropical; frost sensitive
tip: Pinch growing tips to encourage bushier plants.

name: Vietnamese Mint
depth: Plant rooted cuttings at previous soil level
tip: Excellent container plant where its spreading growth can be controlled.

name: Thai Basil
tip: Pinch flower spikes to extend leafy growth.

name: Holy Basil
tip: Frequent tip harvesting encourages branching.

name: Curry Leaf
climate: Subtropical to tropical; protect from hard frost
tip: Grow in a large pot in colder districts so it can be sheltered in winter.

name: Galangal
tip: Rich soil and steady moisture support strong rhizome growth.

name: Ginger
harvest: Young ginger from about 5-6 months; mature rhizomes 8-10 months
tip: Reduce watering as foliage yellows before mature harvest.

name: Cardamom
depth: Shallow; crown at soil level for divisions
harvest: Established plants may flower and fruit after several years
tip: Protect from drying winds and strong afternoon sun.

name: Saffron Crocus
water: Low to moderate; keep relatively dry during dormancy
tip: Harvest the red stigmas promptly when flowers open.

name: Catnip
tip: Cut back after flowering to encourage fresh growth.

name: Lemon Balm
tip: Can spread readily; containers make it easier to contain.

name: Pineapple Sage
climate: Warm temperate to subtropical; frost tender
tip: Prune after flowering or frost damage to encourage new growth.

name: Garlic Chives
tip: Cut leaves near the base and allow clumps to regrow.

name: Feverfew
tip: Deadhead if you want to limit self-seeding.

name: Echinacea
harvest: Flowers from established plants; roots generally after multiple seasons
tip: Good drainage is important, especially through winter.

name: Comfrey
tip: Choose the site carefully because established roots are difficult to remove.

name: Yarrow
tip: Divide crowded clumps every few years.

name: Valerian
harvest: Roots generally after at least one full growing season
tip: Provide moisture-retentive but well-drained soil.

name: Wormwood
tip: Grow in well-drained soil and prune to keep plants compact.

name: Aloe Vera
depth: Set crown just above soil level
water: Low; allow soil to dry between watering
harvest: Mature outer leaves once plant is established
climate: Warm frost-free conditions; protect from frost
tip: Excellent drainage is essential to prevent root rot.

name: Goji Berry
harvest: Fruit commonly from second or third year
tip: Prune to maintain an open framework and make fruit easier to pick.

name: Currant
depth: Plant at nursery level or slightly deeper depending on type
harvest: Fruit from established bushes, usually summer
climate: Cool to temperate; winter chill beneficial
tip: Protect ripening fruit from birds with netting where needed.

name: Gooseberry
harvest: Fruit from established bushes, generally summer
tip: Prune for an open centre to improve airflow and picking access.

name: Boysenberry
propagation: Young plants, tip layers or suckers
tip: Train canes on a trellis and remove spent fruiting canes after harvest.

name: Mulberry
harvest: Fruit from established trees in spring to summer depending on climate
climate: Temperate to subtropical depending on variety
tip: Allow enough room for the mature canopy and fruit drop.

name: Persimmon
depth: Plant at nursery soil level with graft above soil
water: Regular while establishing and during fruit development
climate: Temperate to warm temperate; winter chill helps many cultivars
tip: Thin very heavy fruit sets to reduce branch stress.

name: Pomegranate
harvest: Late summer to autumn on established plants
climate: Warm temperate to subtropical; tolerates dry summers
tip: Best fruiting occurs with plenty of sun and a warm ripening season.

name: Quince
tip: Fruit is usually harvested when fully coloured and aromatic.

name: Loquat
water: Regular while establishing and during fruit development
harvest: Late winter to spring depending on climate
tip: Grafted cultivars give more predictable fruit quality than seedlings.

name: Feijoa
water: Regular during establishment and fruit development
climate: Cool temperate to subtropical; tolerates light frost
tip: Plant compatible cultivars nearby where cross-pollination is recommended.

name: Guava
harvest: Season varies with climate; often warmer months
climate: Subtropical to tropical; some types tolerate mild cool periods
tip: Pruning keeps trees compact and encourages accessible new fruiting growth.

name: Papaya
harvest: Often 9-14 months from seed in warm conditions
climate: Tropical to subtropical; highly frost sensitive
tip: Avoid waterlogged soil and protect plants from strong winds.
